title: Localization-compatible transport of a universal derived pair and its counit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C',\mathcal L,\mathcal L',\mathcal H,\mathcal H'$ be categories in a sufficiently large common universe [def-nagata-category]. Let $W,W'$ be classes of morphisms of $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ and let $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal L$, $Q':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal L'$ be localizations in the functor-category sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Let $e:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal C':i$ be inverse equivalences with triangle-compatible unit and counit, with $e(W)\subset W'$ and $i(W')\subset W$. Then there are inverse equivalences $d:\mathcal L\rightleftarrows\mathcal L':j$ and natural isomorphisms $dQ\cong Q'e$ and $jQ'\cong Qi$. Their units and counits are the unique localized lifts of those of $e,i$; their inverse and triangle identities hold compatibly with these comparisons.

Let $t:\mathcal H\rightleftarrows\mathcal H':u$ be another pair of inverse equivalences, let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal H$, $G:\mathcal C'\to\mathcal H'$ be functors, and fix a natural isomorphism $\sigma:tF\cong Ge$. Suppose $(L,\varepsilon)$ is a universal total left derived pair along $Q$: $L:\mathcal L\to\mathcal H$, $\varepsilon:LQ\to F$, and for every $H:\mathcal L\to\mathcal H$ the map $\operatorname{Nat}(H,L)\to\operatorname{Nat}(HQ,F)$, $\alpha\mapsto\varepsilon\circ(\alpha Q)$, is bijective. This specifies the universal-pair convention of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Put $L'=tLj$. The composite $\gamma:L'Q'=tLjQ'\xrightarrow{\sim}tLQi\xrightarrow{t\varepsilon i}tFi\xrightarrow{\sigma i}Gei\xrightarrow{\sim}G$, using the counit $ei\cong1$, is natural and makes $(L',\gamma)$ a universal total left derived pair along $Q'$. More precisely, for every $H':\mathcal L'\to\mathcal H'$ the composite bijection
$$\operatorname{Nat}(H',tLj)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(uH'd,L)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(uH'dQ,F)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(H'Q',G)$$
is exactly $\alpha\mapsto\gamma\circ(\alpha Q')$. The comparison $L'd\cong tL$ obtained from $jd\cong1$ intertwines $\gamma$ and $t\varepsilon$ under $dQ\cong Q'e$ and $\sigma$. In particular invertibility of the counit on a specified class of objects is preserved by this transport. No exactness, adjunction, tensor, boundedness, or flatness assumptions are required beyond the hypotheses explicitly stated.

proof.text: Write composition right to left, and choose the given equivalence data as $\eta:1\xrightarrow{\sim}ie$, $\theta:ei\xrightarrow{\sim}1$, with $\theta_e\circ e\eta=1_e$ and $i\theta\circ\eta_i=1_i$. Since $Q'e$ inverts $W$ and $Qi$ inverts $W'$, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] supplies $d,j$ and comparisons $a:dQ\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'e$, $b:jQ'\xrightarrow{\sim}Qi$. No calculus-of-fractions condition on $W,W'$ is used.

source.place: Tags 04VG / 04VK, lemma-properties-left-localization / lemma-properties-right-localization; functor-category strengthening stated in the cited node, clause (1)

proof.text: Put $c=b_e\circ j(a):jdQ\xrightarrow{\sim}Qie$ and $f=a_i\circ d(b):djQ'\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'ei$. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], lift $c^{-1}\circ Q\eta$ uniquely to $U:1_{\mathcal L}\xrightarrow{\sim}jd$ and lift $Q'\theta\circ f$ uniquely to $V:dj\xrightarrow{\sim}1_{\mathcal L'}$. Thus $c\circ U_Q=Q\eta$ and $V_{Q'}=Q'\theta\circ f$. The lifts are isomorphisms because the same clause lifts inverses and preserves composites and identities. This specifies the uniqueness relative to $a,b$ intended by the statement.

source.place: Tags 04VG / 04VK; cited node clause (2), including lifting isomorphisms and composition

proof.text:
Check the triangle identities after precomposing with $Q$ or $Q'$, which detects equality by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Explicitly, for every $X\in\mathcal C$ and $Y\in\mathcal C'$ the conjugated components are
$$a_X\circ V_{dQX}\circ d(U_{QX})\circ a_X^{-1}=Q'(\theta_{eX}\circ e(\eta_X))=1_{Q'eX},$$
$$b_Y\circ j(V_{Q'Y})\circ U_{jQ'Y}\circ b_Y^{-1}=Q(i(\theta_Y)\circ\eta_{iY})=1_{QiY}.$$
For the first equation, naturality of $V$ moves $a_X$ to $dj(a_X)$; inserting $V_{Q'eX}=Q'\theta_{eX}\circ a_{ieX}\circ d(b_{eX})$ cancels $d(c_X)$ against $d(U_{QX})=d(c_X^{-1}\circ Q\eta_X)$, and naturality of $a$ at $\eta_X$ gives the displayed result. For the second, naturality of $U$ at $b_Y$ gives $jd(b_Y)\circ U_{jQ'Y}=U_{QiY}\circ b_Y$; inserting $V_{Q'Y}$ and $c_{iY}\circ U_{QiY}=Q\eta_{iY}$ cancels $j(a_{iY})$, and naturality of $b$ at $\theta_Y$ gives the result. The original triangles finish both equalities. Consequently $(d,j,U,V)$ is an adjoint equivalence compatible with the original one; reversing $U,V$ gives inverse equivalence data.

source.place: Tags 04VG / 04VK; cited node clause (3), equality detection; explicit triangle calculation

proof.text:
Choose triangle-compatible isomorphisms $\rho:1_{\mathcal H}\xrightarrow{\sim}ut$ and $\tau:tu\xrightarrow{\sim}1_{\mathcal H'}$ for the target equivalence. For a test functor $H':\mathcal L'\to\mathcal H'$ define
$$B(\alpha)=\rho_L^{-1}\circ u(tL(U^{-1}))\circ u(\alpha_d):uH'd\longrightarrow L.$$
Its inverse is
$$B^{-1}(\beta)=t(\beta_j)\circ t(uH'(V^{-1}))\circ\tau_{H'}^{-1}.$$
All factors have their displayed source and target and are natural. Substitution gives $B^{-1}B(\alpha)=\alpha$ and $BB^{-1}(\beta)=\beta$: move $\alpha$ or $\beta$ across $U,V$ by naturality and cancel $V_d\circ dU=1$, $jV\circ U_j=1$, $\tau_t\circ t\rho=1$, $u\tau\circ\rho_u=1$. Hence this is the first bijection in the statement, with no derived-functor existence assertion used.

source.place: Agent calculation from the stated naturality and triangle identities; universal-pair convention of derived.tex, definition-right-derived-functor-defined and equation-everywhere

proof.text:
Define $r=Q'\theta\circ a_i:dQi\xrightarrow{\sim}Q'$. The third bijection can be specified in the reverse direction by
$$P(\zeta)=\rho_F^{-1}\circ u(\sigma^{-1})\circ u(\zeta_e)\circ uH'(a):uH'dQ\longrightarrow F.$$
Its inverse sends $\delta:uH'dQ\to F$ to
$$P^{-1}(\delta)=G\theta\circ\sigma_i\circ t(\delta_i)\circ t(uH'(r^{-1}))\circ\tau_{H'Q'}^{-1}.$$
Indeed $r_e\circ dQ\eta=a$ follows from naturality of $a$ and $\theta_e\circ e\eta=1$; also $i\theta\circ\eta_i=1$. Substitution in $P^{-1}P$ and $PP^{-1}$, using these two identities and the $\rho,\tau$ triangles, cancels all inserted equivalence isomorphisms, leaving respectively $\zeta$ and $\delta$. This proves the required bijection rather than assuming invariance of Kan extensions.

source.place: Agent calculation from the stated naturality and triangle identities; universal-pair convention of derived.tex, definition-right-derived-functor-defined and equation-everywhere

proof.text:
Let $L'=tLj$ and put
$$\gamma=G\theta\circ\sigma_i\circ t(\varepsilon_i)\circ tL(b):L'Q'\longrightarrow G,\qquad k=tL(U^{-1}):L'd\xrightarrow{\sim}tL.$$
They are natural composites. Their precise compatibility is
$$\gamma_e\circ L'(a)=\sigma\circ t\varepsilon\circ k_Q.$$
To check it substitute $b_e\circ j(a)=Q\eta\circ U_Q^{-1}$ from step 2. The left side becomes $G\theta_e\circ\sigma_{ie}\circ t\varepsilon_{ie}\circ tLQ\eta\circ k_Q$. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ changes the middle two factors to $tF\eta\circ t\varepsilon$; naturality of $\sigma$ then leaves $G(\theta_e\circ e\eta)\circ\sigma\circ t\varepsilon\circ k_Q$, which is the right side.

source.place: Agent calculation from the stated naturality and triangle identities; universal-pair convention of derived.tex, definition-right-derived-functor-defined and equation-everywhere

proof.text:
For $\alpha:H'\to L'$ set $\zeta=\gamma\circ\alpha_{Q'}$. Naturality of $\alpha$ along $a$ and the equality in step 6 give
$$P(\zeta)=\rho_F^{-1}\circ u(\sigma^{-1})\circ u(\gamma_e\circ\alpha_{Q'e})\circ uH'(a)
=\rho_F^{-1}\circ ut\varepsilon\circ u(k_Q)\circ u(\alpha_{dQ})
=\varepsilon\circ B(\alpha)_Q.$$
The last equality is naturality of $\rho$. Thus $P^{-1}\circ(\beta\mapsto\varepsilon\circ\beta_Q)\circ B$ is exactly $\alpha\mapsto\gamma\circ\alpha_{Q'}$. The middle map is bijective by the universal-pair hypothesis, and steps 4--5 give inverse maps for the outer two. This proves universality and identifies the entire displayed composite bijection with the specified counit map.

source.place: Agent calculation from the stated naturality and triangle identities; universal-pair convention of derived.tex, definition-right-derived-functor-defined and equation-everywhere

proof.text: For each $X\in\mathcal C$, the compatibility in step 6 expresses $\gamma_{eX}$ as $t(\varepsilon_X)$ conjugated by the isomorphisms $L'(a_X)$, $\sigma_X$, and $k_{QX}$. A functor takes inverses to inverses; conversely, if $t(h)$ is invertible, then $h=\rho^{-1}\circ ut(h)\circ\rho$ is invertible. Hence $\gamma_{eX}$ is invertible if and only if $\varepsilon_X$ is. For a general $Y\in\mathcal C'$, its defining composite gives invertibility of $\gamma_Y$ if and only if that of $\varepsilon_{iY}$; the isomorphism $\theta_Y:e(iY)\to Y$ identifies these with the corresponding replete classes. This proves the last assertion and completes all clauses without extra homological hypotheses.
